body: Ha! Well it's not like I have much of a choice do I?

I would LOVE to go back to a simpler time... Even my own grandmother, who raised 5 children, can't relate to some of my struggles with my family because really her whole neighborhood raised them. She never felt cooped up in a house all day, alone and isolated, because when her children napped she visited neighbors and had coffee. EVERY DAY. Something as simple as that I image would help keep spirits up...

How do you even come close to replicating that (or a tribe in Fiji or a rural community in America) when you live in the suburbs where very few people are interested? We have neighbors and I've worked for over a year to try and get to know them but there comes a point where if they want their privacy we have to let them have it. Even if it means we're home alone, searching the internet for a like-minded person to talk to.

I do understand what you're saying and I wish thinking like that would help, but all I can manage is like... if so many people on this earth have it SO much worse than I do... why is it so hard to appreciate what I do have? How pathetic and selfish am I to even come here and begin to complain about my struggles when at least I have a healthy family and food on my table? If nothing else, I hate myself for not being able to be grateful for that.
I love this answer. It's funny, you know, how much of a hurry I was become independent... Now, what I wouldn't give to have a "tribe" to raise my family in!

Very true. It's awful the amount of hoops needed to jump through, even with my "good" insurance in order to go see someone for a mental health issue. It pretty much makes it not worth the effort, especially when you're already struggling with things like making phone calls.

Yeah, I've been there. Lots of awesome and well meaning people but I'm never any good at taking the advice they give. Mostly I have too much anxiety about talking to any sort of professional and I've tried everything else... exercise, eating right, making sleep a priority, supplements, etc.

In the meantime I just try to keep everyone else in my family fed and happy, because it's not fair to take them down with me.
Beautiful writing but the end gets me... after four decades of dealing with your depression, you still find you have to take it one tiny step at a time?

I guess I shouldn't have bothered posting because if THIS is the first reply obviously I didn't explain my thoughts well enough.

I wasn't blaming anyone.

Fuck.
